description: StayHub Vietnam RAG corpus for multi-source knowledge augmentation (FCAHR). Structured retrieval chunks with UNESCO citations, interest/persona tags, and tour linkage. Designed for ML.NET semantic retrieval + cultural_fit scoring.

paperMetadata.chunkSchema: id, title, content, cityKeys, interestTags, personaTags, relatedTourIds, chunkType, heritageLevel, source

chunks.title: Hoi An Ancient Town UNESCO heritage significance
chunks.content: Hoi An Ancient Town (UNESCO 1999) preserves a trading port from the 15th-19th centuries with Japanese Bridge, merchant houses, and assembly halls. Lantern festivals and pedestrian evenings support slow cultural tourism. Best for culture, photography, and food-focused itineraries.

chunks.title: Ha Long Bay karst seascape and cruise tourism
chunks.content: Ha Long Bay UNESCO site features ~1,600 limestone islands. Overnight luxury cruises combine cave visits (Sung Sot), kayaking, and onboard dining. Elderly travelers should select cruises with elevator cabins; families need life jackets for kayak segments.

chunks.title: Trang An Ninh Binh mixed natural-cultural landscape
chunks.content: Trang An Landscape Complex (UNESCO 2014) offers boat routes through limestone caves and temples. Seated boat tours suit elderly and children. Combine with Mua Cave viewpoint and Hoa Lu ancient capital.

chunks.title: Thang Long Imperial Citadel Hanoi
chunks.content: Central Sector of Thang Long Imperial Citadel (UNESCO 2010) documents Vietnamese dynastic history. Pair with Old Quarter street food walks, Hoan Kiem Lake, and water puppet theatre for city tours.

chunks.title: Complex of Hue Monuments imperial heritage
chunks.content: Hue imperial citadel and royal tombs form a UNESCO ensemble reflecting Nguyen dynasty architecture. Perfume River boat trips and royal cuisine tasting are signature experiences. Electric carts recommended inside the citadel for elderly visitors.

chunks.title: My Son Cham sanctuary near Hoi An
chunks.content: My Son Sanctuary (UNESCO 1999) preserves red-brick Cham tower temples from the 4th-13th centuries. Day trips from Hoi An or Da Nang suit culture-focused travelers. Morning visits avoid heat.

chunks.title: Can Tho / Mekong Delta — heritage
chunks.content: Cai Rang floating market operates at dawn; river tourism needs sun protection and stable footwear.

chunks.title: Can Tho / Mekong Delta — food
chunks.content: Mekong cuisine: Banh Xeo, freshwater fish, coconut candy. Cash preferred at floating vendors.

chunks.title: Can Tho / Mekong Delta — accessibility
chunks.content: Morning boat departures suit elderly; avoid long open-deck midday segments with children.

chunks.title: Can Tho / Mekong Delta — season
chunks.content: Dry season Dec-May lowers flood risk; floating markets busiest before 8 AM.

chunks.title: Phu Quoc Island — heritage
chunks.content: Phu Quoc offers marine parks, Sao Beach white sand, and night market seafood.

chunks.title: Phu Quoc Island — food
chunks.content: Phu Quoc fish sauce and pepper farms support food tourism; try herring salad (goi ca mai).

chunks.title: Phu Quoc Island — accessibility
chunks.content: Resort-based tours reduce mobility strain for elderly; shallow beaches suit families.

chunks.title: Phu Quoc Island — season
chunks.content: Dry season Nov-Apr preferred for beach; monsoon Jun-Oct may restrict boat trips.

chunks.title: Da Lat Central Highlands — heritage
chunks.content: Da Lat temperate climate supports colonial villas, flower gardens, and specialty coffee.

chunks.title: Da Lat Central Highlands — food
chunks.content: Night market street food and avocado ice cream are local highlights.

chunks.title: Da Lat Central Highlands — accessibility
chunks.content: Cloud-hunting requires pre-dawn departures — not ideal for very young children.

chunks.title: Da Lat Central Highlands — season
chunks.content: Year-round cool evenings; bring light jacket even in summer.

chunks.title: Sapa / Lao Cai — heritage
chunks.content: Sapa terraced fields and ethnic minority villages (Hmong, Dao) define cultural trekking.

chunks.title: Sapa / Lao Cai — food
chunks.content: Local cuisine includes thang co and grilled mountain pork; homestays offer authentic meals.

chunks.title: Sapa / Lao Cai — accessibility
chunks.content: Long treks unsuitable for elderly and toddlers; Fansipan cable car is lower-impact alternative.

chunks.title: Sapa / Lao Cai — season
chunks.content: Sep-Nov and Mar-May offer clearer views; winter fog common Dec-Feb.

chunks.title: Da Nang Central Coast — heritage
chunks.content: Da Nang links Dragon Bridge, My Khe Beach, and gateway to Ba Na Hills Golden Bridge.

chunks.title: Da Nang Central Coast — food
chunks.content: Mi Quang noodles and seafood boulevard are culinary anchors.

chunks.title: Da Nang Central Coast — accessibility
chunks.content: Ba Na Hills cable car aids elderly access to hill attractions.

chunks.title: Da Nang Central Coast — season
chunks.content: Beach safety flags critical during Sep-Dec monsoon swells.

chunks.title: Nha Trang / Khanh Hoa — heritage
chunks.content: Nha Trang bay supports island hopping, diving, and Ponagar Cham towers.

chunks.title: Nha Trang / Khanh Hoa — food
chunks.content: Banh Can mini pancakes and fresh seafood define local food identity.

chunks.title: Nha Trang / Khanh Hoa — accessibility
chunks.content: Licensed dive operators required; island day trips with seated transport suit elderly.

chunks.title: Nha Trang / Khanh Hoa — season
chunks.content: Best sea conditions Feb-Aug; typhoon season Oct-Dec may cancel boats.

chunks.title: Ho Chi Minh City — heritage
chunks.content: Saigon blends colonial Notre-Dame area, Ben Thanh Market, and Cu Chi tunnel day trips.

chunks.title: Ho Chi Minh City — food
chunks.content: Street food tours (Banh Mi, Hu Tieu) are signature urban experiences.

chunks.title: Ho Chi Minh City — accessibility
chunks.content: Air-conditioned vehicle tours reduce heat stress for elderly in dry season.

chunks.title: Ho Chi Minh City — season
chunks.content: Hot dry season Mar-May; rainy afternoons May-Nov — plan indoor museums.

chunks.title: Vietnam coastal beach tourism patterns
chunks.content: Key beach clusters: Phu Quoc, Nha Trang, Da Nang, Mui Ne, Phu Quy. Resort packages suit couples; check jellyfish season and lifeguard presence for family beach days.

chunks.title: Mekong and Red River delta river tourism
chunks.content: River tourism spans Cai Rang floating market, Mekong homestays, Perfume River Hue, and Trang An boats. Life jackets and licensed operators are mandatory safety requirements.

chunks.title: Vietnamese intangible cultural heritage for tourists
chunks.content: Water puppetry (Hanoi), Quan Ho folk songs (Bac Ninh), Ca Tru, and lantern festivals (Hoi An) provide accessible cultural entry points for international visitors.

chunks.title: Vietnamese regional cuisine map for tour planning
chunks.content: North: Pho, Bun Cha. Central: Mi Quang, Cao Lau. South: Hu Tieu, Banh Xeo. Street food tours need reputable operators for hygiene-conscious foreign guests.

chunks.title: Vietnam nature and national park tourism
chunks.content: National parks include Cat Ba, Cuc Phuong, Phong Nha-Ke Bang, Bach Ma. Trek difficulty varies; elderly should prefer cable car or boat-based nature experiences.

chunks.title: Adventure tourism safety in Vietnam
chunks.content: Trekking (Sapa), diving (Nha Trang), kayaking (Ha Long), canyoning (Da Lat) require operator licensing. Not recommended for groups with young children or mobility-limited elderly.

chunks.title: Resort and wellness tourism in Vietnam
chunks.content: Cam Ranh and Phu Quoc lead resort/spa offerings; Ha Long luxury cruises combine relaxation with scenery. Honeymoon packages emphasize privacy and spa access.

chunks.title: Photography tourism hotspots Vietnam
chunks.content: Golden hour spots: Hoi An lanterns, Ha Long sunrise decks, Sapa terraces (Sep harvest), Da Lat cloud hunting (Cau Dat 4:30 AM departures).

chunks.title: Urban tourism in Vietnam major cities
chunks.content: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City offer museums, markets, and colonial architecture. Traffic density requires guided transport for first-time foreign visitors.

chunks.title: Foreign visitor etiquette and visa basics
chunks.content: Dress modestly at temples; remove shoes; ask before photographing people. E-visa available for many nationalities; Phu Quoc special zone policies may differ. Tipping not mandatory but appreciated for guides.

chunks.title: Elderly-friendly tour design principles Vietnam
chunks.content: Prefer morning schedules, seated transport, elevator-equipped hotels/cruises, minimal stair climbing. Avoid motorbike street food tours and multi-hour treks. Ha Long cruises and Trang An boats offer seated experiences.

chunks.title: Family travel with children in Vietnam
chunks.content: Theme parks (Ba Na Hills), shallow beaches (Phu Quoc), water puppet shows (Hanoi), and lantern workshops (Hoi An) suit mixed-age groups. Limit dive/trek/motorbike activities.

chunks.title: Group dynamics and fair activity selection
chunks.content: Group tour fairness requires balancing adventure seekers with comfort-preferring members. Itineraries with optional activities (kayak vs deck rest) reduce dissatisfaction variance. River and resort bases offer natural split activity windows.

chunks.title: Vietnam monsoon and typhoon travel advisories
chunks.content: Central coast typhoon risk peaks Sep-Dec affecting Da Nang, Hoi An, Nha Trang boats. Mekong Delta flooding possible Jun-Nov. North winter fog affects Sapa views Dec-Feb.

chunks.title: Phu Quoc 4D3N resort package
chunks.content: Resort stay on Phu Quoc with Sao Beach, Sunset Town, and night market. Ideal beach-relax couples and solo.

chunks.title: Da Lat 3D2N cloud hunting
chunks.content: Youthful Da Lat itinerary: Cau Dat cloud hunting, coffee farms, night market. Culture-nature blend.

chunks.title: Hoi An 2D1N ancient town lanterns
chunks.content: Ancient town walking, Cao Lau tasting, flower lantern release. UNESCO core experience.

chunks.title: Ha Long 2D1N luxury cruise
chunks.content: Overnight bay cruise with cave visits and gala dinner. Premium relax-nature product.

chunks.title: Mekong Delta 2D1N floating market
chunks.content: Cai Rang floating market, fruit orchards, homestay cuisine. River-food-cultural triangle.

chunks.title: Sapa 4D3N village trekking
chunks.content: Cat Cat village, terraced fields, Fansipan option. Adventure-nature; limited elderly fit.

chunks.title: Ninh Binh 2D1N Trang An Mua Cave
chunks.content: Trang An boat, Mua Cave viewpoint, Hoa Lu capital. Accessible nature-culture day trips.

chunks.title: Da Nang 3D2N Dragon Bridge Ba Na
chunks.content: Coastal city, Dragon Bridge show, Ba Na Hills Golden Bridge. Mixed beach-city-theme.

chunks.title: Saigon evening food tour
chunks.content: Motorbike or walking street food: Banh Mi, Hu Tieu, district nightlife. Urban food focus.

chunks.title: Cam Ranh honeymoon 3D2N
chunks.content: Private beach resort, spa, romantic dinner. Couple-relax premium positioning.

chunks.title: Hanoi photo walk 1 day
chunks.content: Old Quarter, Hoan Kiem, Bun Cha, egg coffee photo hunting. Short city-photography product.

chunks.title: Nha Trang island hopping dive
chunks.content: Scuba, Binh Ba Island, Banh Can. Adventure-beach; check child age for diving.

chunks.content: Signature chewy noodles with char siu — UNESCO town food icon.

chunks.title: Mekong Banh Xeo
chunks.content: Crispy turmeric crepe with herbs — delta street food staple.

chunks.title: Hanoi Bun Cha
chunks.content: Grilled pork with noodles — Obama-era global fame dish.

chunks.title: Nha Trang Banh Can
chunks.content: Mini clay-oven cakes with dipping sauce.

chunks.title: Da Nang Mi Quang
chunks.content: Turmeric noodles with minimal broth — central Vietnam icon.

chunks.title: Saigon Banh Mi

chunks.title: Sapa bamboo rice
chunks.content: Sticky rice in bamboo tube — ethnic highland specialty.

chunks.title: Hue lemongrass skewers
chunks.content: Royal city finger food with peanut sauce.

chunks.title: Fresh spring rolls national
chunks.content: Universal light appetizer — elderly-friendly food format.

chunks.title: Vietnamese coffee culture
chunks.content: Robusta drip coffee and egg coffee — Da Lat cafe tourism.

chunks.title: Hoi An flat terrain elderly access
chunks.content: Ancient town core is pedestrian flat — wheelchair partial access.

chunks.title: Ha Long cruise mobility
chunks.content: Select operators with cabin elevators and minimal kayak-only routes.

chunks.title: Phu Quoc resort accessibility
chunks.content: International resorts offer pool lifts and ground-floor rooms.

chunks.title: Da Nang family theme access
chunks.content: Ba Na Hills cable car eliminates uphill climb for strollers.

chunks.title: Hanoi rest-stop walking tours
chunks.content: Old Quarter tours with cafe breaks every 30 minutes recommended.
